messages:
PagerBot: :rotating_light: Pager: High-severity alert — sudden quality regressions correlated with cost-based routing increase. Metric: 'generation_quality_score' down 28% for traffic tagged 'prod-eu' since 2132107600. Affected customer count: ~12 (top impacted: AcmePay). Routing policy: cost-led-fallback v2.0. Severity: P1.
Maria C: Ack. I'm oncall. Looking at dashboards now.
Ajay P: I'm awake, will join. Maria — do you see a model variant spike to a cheap quantized variant?
Maria C: Yes — seeing a jump from redwood-base-1.3 -> redwood-lite-4q over the last 12m. Traffic percent went from 2% -> 47% for prod-eu.
Noor S: Paging SRE lead @Noor S for routing config check. Could be policy evaluation bug that prefers cheapest compatible model incorrectly.
Diego M: @Maria can you pull the policy eval trace? I want the decision chain.
Maria C: Pasting relevant eval (sanitized):
```
policy: cost-led-fallback v2.0
input: customer=prod-eu, latency_slo=200ms, budget_signal=low
candidates: redwood-base-1.3 (cost=0.12, score=0.92), redwood-lite-4q (cost=0.03, score=0.65)
eval: choose variant with min(cost) subject to latency and compatibility -> selected redwood-lite-4q
notes: fallback threshold misconfigured (threshold=0.0) -> effectively no quality floor
```
Ajay P: That threshold=0.0 is the smoking gun. Should have been >=0.75. Who last changed the policy?
Emma R: I rotated the policy last week to optimize spend for a trial cohort (PR #4123). I unintentionally left the quality_floor at 0 for the cost-path. Sorry.
Noor S: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Freeze cost-led-fallback routing, 2) Force-pin prod-eu to baseline variant redwood-base-1.3, 3) Roll forward a corrected policy with quality_floor=0.75, 4) Notify affected customers.
Maria C: I can apply steps 1+2 now. Executing temporary override:
```
# disable cost path
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/policies/cost-led-fallback/freeze -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# pin route
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/routing/overrides -d '{"scope":"prod-eu","variant":"redwood-base-1.3","expires":"+30m"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```
Maria C: Executed. Policy freeze returned 200. Route override applied.
Diego M: Observability: generating quick sanity checks. Running sample eval requests to prod-eu.
(2m later)
Diego M: Quick samples: outputs look back to expected quality for AcmePay test cases. quality_score median jumped from 0.46 -> 0.89.
Ajay P: Great. Now we need the permanent fix: revert or patch policy PR to set quality_floor and add unit tests. Emma, can you push patch and coordinate canary?
Emma R: On it. I'll open PR to set quality_floor=0.75 and add a policy regression test + deploy in canary for 15m.
Noor S: I'll run a post-incident checklist: confirm freeze is holding, audit recent policy changes, and prepare communication.
Customer Ops Bot: Notifying Customer Success: impacted customers list generated (12). Sending email draft to CS team for customer outreach.
Maria C: Monitoring key signals: token latency OK, error rate stable, quality metrics returning to baseline. Will keep override for 30m until PR is live and validated.
Ajay P: Logging timeline for postmortem. Please capture: root cause = policy config regression (quality_floor omitted) + lack of policy unit tests for fallbacks. Secondary cause = too-aggressive automated spend optimization without guard rails.
Diego M: We should also add an automated alert for sudden variant-shift > 10% within 10m for production routes. Filing infra ticket.
Emma R: PR #4238 opened: sets quality_floor=0.75, adds tests, and adds a canary flag. Deploying to canary now.
(10m later)
Emma R: Canary deploy looks good. Metrics stable. Merging and rolling to prod in 5m.
Maria C: Rolling policy unfreeze and removing the temporary override after confirmed merge.
Maria C: Override removed at 2132113120. Policy thawed.
Diego M: Post-merge validation: variant distribution back to expected: redwood-base-1.3 -> 95%, redwood-lite-4q -> 3%. Quality scores stable.
Noor S: Customer impact summary draft: 12 customers briefly routed to low-cost variant; duration median 18 minutes; visible quality regressions for some prompts; no data exfiltration; remediation applied with override + policy fix. Recommended next steps: postmortem, alert for variant drift, stricter preflight checks for policy changes, and an emergency kill-switch for cost-path.
Ajay P: Assign postmortem owners: Emma (policy changes), Diego (observability/alerting), Maria (mitigation runbook). Please add timeline, root cause, customer impact, and follow-ups.
Customer Ops Bot: CS outreach messages queued for top 3 customers (AcmePay, TravelBee, FinLedger).
Maria C: Closing pager for now. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and will escalate if anything reappears. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
Emma R: Thanks team. Writing up postmortem template now.
Noor S: Good catch and fast mitigation. We'll review policy rollout process to prevent similar regressions.
metadata: incident: cost-routing-variant-drift; severity: P1; mitigation: routing override + policy patch; followups: postmortem, alert, unit-tests, kill-switch
